Lexemes, being the result of mental analysis and categorization of the extra lingual reality, have the following main features: 
Lexical words (Lexemes)
3
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
Arbitrariness
Conventionality
Việt Đức

This property describes the fact that a lexeme (a linguistic form) usually lacks any physical correspondence with the objects, states, processes, etc. of the reality to which it refers. 
Arbitrariness
a
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
E.g The word “Book”
No describe the shape, colour, or function
The sound form /bʊk/ versus the concept of the book is arbitrary
Arbitrariness
Việt Đức

The arbitrariness of words is also called conventionality. It will be used here to refer to the fact that lexemes are a matter of agreement and convention accepted by the members of a given community. 
Conventionality
b
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
E.g The sounds woof-woof or gâu gâu
Woof-woof → dog’s sound (English) 
Gâu gâu → dog’s sound (Vietnamese)
Conventionality
Việt Đức

These are word forms that differ in grammatical meaning. 
Grammatical words:
4
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
E.g The sounds woof-woof or gâu gâu
E.g. shoot, shoots, shooting, shot. 
E.g. shot as past tense or past participle.
Việt Đức

One word form can have different (related or unrelated) meanings
Semantic words (Sememes)
5
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
E.g. The single word form "shoot" encompasses multiple distinct sememes: 
(1) to fire a gun
(2) to injure or kill with a missile
(3) to kick or hit a ball toward a goal
(4) to record film footage.
Việt Đức

Motivation refers to the basis for forming a new word or meaning. It can be phonetic, morphological, or semantic.
Semantic words (Sememes) - Motivation
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
E.g The sounds woof-woof or gâu gâu
(a) Phonetic motivation: the word imitates a sound existing in the extra-lingual reality 
cock-a-doodle-doo; 
woof/bark; 
quack.
Việt Đức

(b) Morphological motivation: the new word is based on the morphemes already existing in a language 
Example:
rethink (re+think)
writer (write+er)
bedroom (bed+room) 
Semantic words (Sememes) - Motivation
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
Việt Đức

(c) Semantic motivation: the new word is based on an already existing word, and the new meaning is derived from the original 
Example:
one – a hand (a human hand → a hand of a clock)
 to see (to perceive with eyes → to understand)
black (of dark colour → bad/illegal)
Semantic words (Sememes) - Motivation
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)

b. Root vs. Affixational

3.1.2.3 Inflection versus Derivation

A word has four main characteristics that define its structure and grammatical behavior.
Four characteristics of the words
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
An uninterruptible unit
Consists of one or more morphemes
Occurs in phrase structures
Belongs to a specific word class
Việt Đức

An uninterruptible unit
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
Ex: blackbird
 black very bird
No independent linguistic element can be inserted into the interior structure of a word without destroying its integrity
Việt Đức
Ex: pickpocket

Consists of one or more morphemes
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
Ex: book
books
Words range from monomorphemic forms to polymorphemic constructions.
Việt Đức
Ex: box
boxes

Occurs in phrase structures
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
Ex: a beautiful girl 
Words typically combine syntactically to form higher-level phrases
Việt Đức
Ex: a small black cat

Belongs to a specific word class
Source: BÀI GIẢNG TV-NN HỌC CHO SINH VIÊN, Pavlík (2017)
Example:
The young teacher speaks clearly.
A heavy storm arrived suddenly.
Every word is classified into a part of speech based on its syntactic function and distributional properties. 
The             young        teacher     speaks     clearly. 
[determiner]   [adjective]     [noun]        [verb]      [adverb]

[determiner]   [adjective]     [noun]     [verb]        [adverb]

ROOT
Như Ý

Roots
The CENTRAL morpheme of a word that carries its main lexical meaning and forms the core part to which other morphemes may be added. 
Free roots
A root that can stand alone.
Bound roots 
A root that cannot occur independently as a word.
help in helpless
happy in unhappy
-clude in include
-port in transport

Như Ý

Affixes
a BOUND morpheme attached to a root, stem, or base.  
Derivational affixes: Changes meaning or word class.
kind → unkind
            kindness
 Inflectional affixes: Grammatical change (tense, number).
cat →cats
play → played

over = overweight

super = supernatural

COMPOUNDING
Compounding is a process of creating new words by combining at least two root morphemes.

Containing only two root morphemes
COMPLEX COMPOUNDING
Containing more than two morphemes

 sugar-free = sugar + free
